BackendAdd.description: The body of `POST /pools/{pool}/backends`: the backend to add to the pool at runtime.

BackendPatch.description:
The body of `PATCH /pools/{pool}/backends/{addr}`: the new operator state, one of `enabled`,
`draining` or `disabled`. `draining` and `disabled` stop new-session selection while existing
sessions keep running.

ConfigSaved.description: What `PUT /config/file` answers once the file is written.

applied.description: Whether the reload took the new file within the wait (5 s).

etag.description: The ETag of the file as saved; send it as `If-Match` on the next edit.

note.description: Present when `applied` is false: what that does and does not mean.

revision.description: The revision counter of the file as saved; the `base` of the next edit.

saved.description: The file was written. It is the file that changed, whether or not the reload took it (`applied`).

ErrorBody.description: The JSON error shape the config routes use.

code.description: A stable code for the cases a client branches on; today only `stale`.

error.description: What went wrong, in one sentence.
error.example: the config file changed since you read it

FeatureRow.description: One feature flag, as `GET /features` lists it.

apply.description: When a change takes effect: `live` or only at the next `startup`.

available.description: Whether this build contains the code the flag switches.

impact.description: What happens to connections that are already open.

override.description:
Which way a controller override may flip the flag. `off_only` flags open new network
exposure, so a stolen token cannot switch them on.

protection.description: Turning the flag off removes a protection (rate limits, ACLs), so an override of it needs an expiry.

risk.description: What turning the flag off costs, in one sentence.

since.description: The config `schema_version` that introduced the flag.

source.description:
Where `value` comes from: the built-in `default`, the `features:` section of the config
(`config`), a controller `override`, or the `build` (the binary was built without the code
the flag switches).

wired.description: Whether the runtime consults the flag yet. An unwired flag is accepted and reported but changes nothing.

RouteHintReq.description:
The body of `POST /route-hint`: a short-lived `src_ip` to pool mapping that listeners with
`route_hint: true` consult before their route list.

pool.description: The pool to send that client's next connection to.

src_ip.description: The client address the hint is for.

ttl_sec.description: How long the hint lives, 1 to 3600 seconds.

fallback.description:
The live instance runs the previous version because the current file
failed validation at the last scan.

loaded.description:
Whether this module is actually loaded into the live registry right
now (a file can exist on disk but have failed its last scan — e.g. a
hash-pin mismatch — in which case this is `false`).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file, lowercase hex.

ok.description: Always `true`: a failure is a `422` with an `ErrorBody` instead.

schema_version.description: The `schema_version` of the document that was checked.

WebReply.description: The resolved `web:` section, as `wayhouse-web-sync` reads it.

internal_bind.description: Loopback address of the generated `via: wayhouse` listeners.

pool.description: The pool the entry node's :80/:443 listeners send to (Caddy's).

trusted_proxy.description: CIDRs Caddy trusts PROXY headers from, besides loopback.

health_path.description: Path for the active health check, when set.

oneOf.description: The certificate and key files of the site, when it has them.

upstream_tls.description: `"verify"`, `"skip"` or `{"ca_file": path}`; absent means plain HTTP to the upstream.

upstreams.description:
Each upstream is `{"addr": "ip:port"}`, or `{"pool": name, "via": "direct"|"wayhouse"}`
(`via: wayhouse` also carries `local`, the generated loopback listener).

bearer.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the value of `settings.admin.auth_token`. With no token configured the API is open.

info.description: The HTTP API every `wayhouse` proxy serves on `settings.admin.listen` (default `127.0.0.1:9900`). It reads the live state, changes backends, drains the instance, and reads or replaces the config file.
info.title: wayhouse proxy admin API

post.description: Marks the instance draining: `/readyz` starts failing so a load balancer stops sending new clients, while the data path keeps serving. Sessions in flight are never closed by this. Wait for `active_conns` to fall, then stop the process (`SIGTERM`). Undo it with `POST /admin/undrain`.
post.summary: Take the instance out of rotation

get.description: Every `.wasm` file in `settings.sniffers.dir` with its SHA-256, size, and whether it is loaded now. A file can exist but not be loaded, for example after a hash-pin mismatch.

409.description: This instance has no `settings.sniffers` block; turning sniffing on from nothing needs a restart.

post.description: The body is the raw bytes of a `.wasm` module, at most 8 MiB. It is validated, checked against the `settings.sniffers.modules` pins when the instance has any, written atomically to `settings.sniffers.dir/<name>.wasm`, and a reload picks it up. The module it replaces is kept for `rollback`. Nothing is written when a check fails. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.sniffer_upload`.

parameters.description: The module name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`. The file is stored as `<name>.wasm`.
parameters.name: name

400.description: The name is invalid, or the bytes are not a loadable sniffer module.

409.description: No `settings.sniffers` block, or the instance pins its modules and this name or hash is not listed (`pinned:`).

413.description: The body is larger than the module limit.

500.description: The file could not be written.

delete.description: Removes `<name>.wasm` and the kept previous version, then a reload drops it from the live registry. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.sniffer_upload`.

500.description: The file could not be removed.

post.description: Swaps `<name>.wasm` with the kept previous version, so a second rollback undoes the first. Exactly one previous version is kept. On an instance that pins its modules it only works when the previous version's SHA-256 is pinned. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.sniffer_upload`.

409.description: No `settings.sniffers` block, or the previous version's hash is not pinned (`pinned:`).

post.description: Clears the draining mark; `/readyz` passes again if a listener is configured.
post.summary: Put the instance back into rotation

get.description: A plain-text view of the live snapshot: the global limits, each listener with its bind address, protocol, route count and the options it has switched on, and each pool with its backends. It is a summary for people; use `GET /config/file` for the file itself.

The config file the proxy runs from, with its ETag. Inline secrets are masked in the body (a value such as `__wayhouse_redacted_admin_token__` stands in for the secret), and saving the shown text keeps them. A proxy started with `--controller` has no file and answers `404`.

parameters.description: `1` (or `true`) returns the copy the last write kept of the file before it.
parameters.name: previous

ETag.description: Send it as `If-Match` when you save an edit of this text.

X-Config-Revision.description: The file's revision counter; the alternative to the ETag, as `?base=` on a save.

404.description: This proxy has no config file, or `previous=1` and no earlier version is kept yet.

422.description: The file does not parse, so its secrets cannot be masked; fix it on the host.

put.description: Replaces the file with the YAML body if it is still the version you read, then triggers a reload. Off unless the proxy was started with `--allow-config-write`. Name the version you edited with `If-Match` (the ETag of the read) or `?base=` (its `X-Config-Revision`). The old file is kept and can be read with `GET /config/file?previous=1`. The body is limited to 1 MiB.

parameters.description: The `X-Config-Revision` of the version you edited, instead of `If-Match`.
parameters.name: base

200.description: Saved. `applied` says whether the reload took it within five seconds.

403.description: Config writes are switched off: start the proxy with `--allow-config-write`.

404.description: This proxy has no config file.

409.description: The file changed since you read it (`code: stale`). Read it again and redo the edit.

422.description: The new text does not validate; the file is unchanged.

503.description: The file or its directory is not writable.

get.description: The JSON Schema the config is validated against, the same one the controller serves. The header `X-Config-Schema-Version` carries the highest `schema_version` this build accepts.
get.summary: JSON Schema of a config document

post.description: Parses and validates the YAML in the body with the same code as a reload, and applies nothing. Nothing is read from the running config: a pool a listener names has to be in the document itself.

example.error: invalid configuration: listener game: route 0: unknown pool survival

422.description: The document does not parse or fails validation; `error` names the key and the reason.

get.description: Every proxy feature flag with its effective value and where the value comes from. The flags and what they do are in the Manual.

200.description: All flags of the proxy scope.

get.description: Answers `ok` while the process runs. It is the only route that needs no bearer token, so a load balancer or a container runtime can probe it.
Every `wayhouse_*` series in the Prometheus text exposition format. The series are listed in the Reference.
The OpenAPI 3.1 document these pages are generated from, as served by the build you are talking to. Use it to generate a client or to check what a particular version supports.
One block per pool: the pool name and balancer, then each backend with its health, operator state (`enabled`, `draining`, `disabled`) and the number of live sessions.

200.description: Plain text, one line per pool and per backend, tab separated.

post.description: Adds the address to the pool at runtime. The edit lives in the runtime overlay, so it survives a config reload. The call requests a reload and returns; the backend joins when that reload completes (normally within a moment, so an immediate `PATCH` of it can still answer `404`), and the health checker corrects its state within one interval. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.backends` (on by default).

parameters.description: The pool name, as in the config.
parameters.name: pool

post.summary: Add a backend to a pool

delete.description: Works whether the backend came from the config file or from an earlier `POST`. Sessions already on it keep running; it just stops being chosen. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.backends`.
delete.summary: Remove a backend from a pool

patch.description: `draining` and `disabled` stop new sessions from choosing the backend; sessions already on it keep running. `enabled` puts it back. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.backends`.

parameters.description: The backend address as `ip:port` (URL-encode an IPv6 address's brackets and colons).
parameters.name: addr

400.description: `state` is not one of enabled, draining, disabled, or `addr` is not an `ip:port`.

404.description: Unknown pool, or the backend is not in the pool.

get.description: `200` when at least one listener is configured and the instance is not draining; `503` otherwise. Point a load balancer's health check here: `POST /admin/drain` makes it fail on purpose.

503.description: Draining (`draining`) or no listener configured (`not ready`).

post.description: Records a short-lived `src_ip` to pool mapping, which listeners with `route_hint: true` consult before their route list. A launcher or control plane calls it just before it sends a player to the proxy. The hint expires on its own. Needs the feature flag `admin_write.route_hint`.

requestBody.description: The client address, the pool, and how long the hint lives.

400.description: `src_ip` is not an IP address, `ttl_sec` is outside 1 to 3600, or the pool does not exist.

post.summary: Push a route hint for a client address

get.description: Every live proxied TCP connection and UDP session, oldest id first: id, transport, listener, client and local address, the pool and backend chosen, and the age. A point-in-time list; a session that has ended is absent. The filters match exactly.

parameters.description: Only sessions of this listener (exact name).
parameters.name: listener

parameters.description: Only sessions routed to this pool (exact name).
parameters.name: pool

parameters.description: Only sessions from this client IP address.
parameters.name: src

text/plain.example:
sessions=1
  7	tcp	game	peer=203.0.113.9:51234	local=198.51.100.1:7777	pool=game	backend=10.0.0.5:7777	age=12.3s

200.description: Plain text. The first line is `sessions=<count>`; each session follows on its own line, tab separated.

get.description: What `wayhouse-web-sync` reads to build Caddy's configuration: where Caddy listens and, per site, its hosts, upstreams in final form and TLS settings. `404` when the config has no `web:` section.
